calendar.name: T623
calendar.text: I hope you’re happy with your new sod house, neighbor. We built it quickly because we worked together. That's what neighbors do.

calendar.name: NoBuild
calendar.text:
Neighbor, please let me and some
other folks help you build a barn.
Your animals need some shade and
protection from the rain. 
You should also dig a well soon.
By July, the creek will be almost dry.

calendar.name: NoWM
calendar.text: It's very difficult to carry water in pails all the way from the creek. Now the creek is nearly dry. Our neighbors say that if we buy a windmill, they’ll help us build it and dig a well.

calendar.name: OnlyBuild
calendar.text: I'm tired of carrying water from the creek far away. Can we please build the windmill you've bought?

calendar.name: NoBarn
calendar.text: Neighbor, please let me and some other folks help you build a barn. Your animals need some shade and protection from rain.

calendar.name: WMEOG
calendar.text: Hello, neighbor. I see that you still have no well or windmill. If you buy a windmill, I'll help you build it and dig a well.

calendar.name: AnimD
calendar.text: The cold weather killed all your animals. Since you don't have a dairy cow, it will cost $10 dollars a month to buy milk from a neighbor.

calendar.name: AfterTorn
calendar.text: Hello, neighbor. Looks like the tornado left your farm in pretty bad shape! If you need help repairing  things, just ask  for it!

calendar.name: BuildFence
calendar.text: You need to build fence.

calendar.name: Rep
calendar.text:
That was some tornado, neighbor.
If I were you, I'd fix everything that was
damaged as soon as possible. 
In another month or two, it will be too cold
to work outside. Anyway, your animals won't 
make it through the winter without a barn.

calendar.name: Fire
calendar.text: My crops were destroyed in the prairie fire, too.  We'll have to plow and plant again, if there's enough time.

calendar.name: GrH
calendar.text: Oh no, all our crops were eaten! Now we'll have to plow and plant again, if there's enough time.

calendar.name: NoFence1
calendar.text:
A herd of cattle trampled some of your crops. In the old country, you could have built a wooden fence around your field, but you won't find much wood around here!
 I've heard about a new kind of fence, but it's not in the general store's catalog yet.

calendar.name: NoFence2
calendar.text: A herd of cattle trampled some of your crops. You need a good fence around your field. I've heard that neighbor Daniel built a fence out of something new, called barbed wire. Maybe it's in the general store's catalog.

calendar.name: NoFence3
calendar.text: A few cattle broke down your wooden fence. They destroyed some of your crops. If you go to the general store and look at the catalog, I think you'll find exactly what you need.

calendar.name: CantBuild
calendar.text:
It's too cold to build anything right now.
You need to wait until early spring.

calendar.name: NothToB
calendar.text: You have nothing to build.

calendar.name: NoM
calendar.text: You don't have enough money to do this.

calendar.name: NoBuy
calendar.text: You don't have enough money to buy this.

calendar.name: LoanRet
calendar.text: Time has come to repay your loan. Make sure to come to the bank to repay your loan by the end of the month.

calendar.name: LoanEnd
calendar.text:
You didn't repay your loan on time, so the bank is taking over your farm. I'm sorry to hear you'll be heading back east.
 I hope you'll come back soon and start over again.

calendar.name: MyHelp
calendar.text: I need your help to finish the work in my field on time.

calendar.name: Startover
calendar.text: Be careful! If you start over all your work will be erased.

calendar.name: NoHouse
calendar.text: Can you hear those folks in town talking? They'd like to meet you. Why don't you come by and say hello?

calendar.name: YesHouse
calendar.text:
Congratulations! You have another son! Your monthly cost of living will increase by five dollars per month. 

My baby's name is:

moneyCrisis.name: NOM1
moneyCrisis.text: You folks are very brave, but no one can survive out here without money to buy food and supplies. I collected $100.00 from your neighbors to help you through the winter. I'm sure you would do the same for us.

moneyCrisis.name: NoM2
moneyCrisis.text: Take money out of the box under your bed.

moneyCrisis.name: NoM3
moneyCrisis.text: After all your hard work, it's a shame not to sell your crops. It's no wonder that you ran out of money. I think you should sell your crops right away.

moneyCrisis.name: NoM4
moneyCrisis.text: Hello, neighbor. You look as though you could use some advice. You can use your homestead claim as security to borrow money from the bank.

moneyCrisis.name: NOM5
moneyCrisis.text: I'm sorry to hear that you're heading back east. We heard that you ran out of money. I collected $50.00 from your neighbors to help pay for your journey. I hope you'll come back next year and try again.

moneyCrisis.name: NOM6
moneyCrisis.text: I'm sorry to hear that you're heading back east. We heard that you ran out of money. I hope you'll come back next year and try again.

field.name: NoPlow1
field.text: There are enough things to do here. You don't have to plow the fields twice and make extra work for yourself.

field.name: NoPlow2
field.text: You planted some crops that you haven't harvested yet. If you plow now, you will destroy all your hard work.

field.name: NoPlow3
field.text: The land is frozen. If you plow now, you could break your plow. It's better to wait until spring.

field.name: Noplow4
field.text: The land is very muddy from all the rain. The plow will sink in the mud. It's better to wait until fall.

field.name: NoPlow5
field.text: Hello, neighbor. I'm glad to see you. It's not time to plant yet. First, you should harvest the last crop that you planted.

field.name: NoPlow6
field.text: I'm waiting for you to sell me your crops. I'll give you a good price.

field.name: FDBK7
field.text: Great. Now that you finished plowing,                 you can start planting.

field.name: StopPlow1
field.text: The summer rains started before you finished  plowing. You have to stop plowing now. Your fields are all muddy.

field.name: StopPlow2
field.text: The ground froze before you finished plowing. You have to stop plowing now. It's starting to snow.

field.name: StopPlow3
field.text:
Your plow broke. The land is very hard in this area. What are you going to do?

      1.  Buy a new steel right away for $50.

      2.  Fix the old plow for free, 
           which takes a few days.

field.name: StopPlow4
field.text: One of your horses is sick. Now you can use only one horse, so your plowing will take twice as long.

field.name: NoMoney
field.text:
I'm sorry. You don't have enough cash
                    to buy a new plow.

field.name: NoPlant1
field.text: You don't have any seeds. Drop by the store to order some. You can look at our catalog which shows the seeds you can buy and the plants you can grow from them.

field.name: NoPlant2
field.text: Soon the hot summer sun will beat down on your fields and dry out your seeds. If I were you, I would plow my land before I plant those seeds.

field.name: NoPlant3
field.text: If you don't plow your land soon, the winds will scatter most of your seeds. Those seeds will grow, but not necessarily on your land.

field.name: NoPlant4
field.text: Hello, neighbor. I'm glad to see you. It's not time to plant yet. First, you should harvest the last crop that you planted.

field.name: NoPlant5
field.text: I think the seed catalog suggested a different season for planting those seeds. If I were you, I would check the catalog.

field.name: NoPlant6
field.text: It's too early to plow or plant your fields, neighbor. The ground is still frozen. Why don't you wait until April, when the ground thaws?

field.name: NoPlant7
field.text:
You can't plant any seeds now, neighbor.
You've already planted all the land you plowed.

field.name: NoPlant8
field.text: I wouldn't plow or plant in the middle of summer, neighbor. The seeds won't grow well now.

field.name: NoHarv1
field.text: Have patience, my friend. Give your plants enough time to grow before you harvest them.

field.name: NoHarv2
field.text: My friend, you have to plant before you can harvest.You can't get something from nothing.

field.name: NoHarv3
field.text: Hello there, neighbor. I see that you still have a bit to learn about farming. You can't harvest your fields before you've even plowed them and planted some seeds.

field.name: StopHarv1
field.text: The summer rains started early this year. They destroyed the rest of your crops. There's no point in harvesting them now.

field.name: StopHarv2
field.text: Winter came early this year. The first frost killed the rest of your crops. There's no point in harvesting them now.

field.name: OneWor
field.text: I'm sorry. You don't have enough money to pay me. I can't work for you if you can't pay me.

field.name: ManyWor
field.text: I'm sorry. You don't have enough money to pay us. We can't work for you if you can't pay us.

field.name: EndHarv
field.text: Now that you've harvested your crops, it's time to sell them. I'll make you an  offer you can't refuse.

field.name: Tractor
field.text: There aren't enough tractors for all of us. Make sure that you have a tractor for each worker you hire.

field.name: FDB18
field.text: You were lucky. The summer rains started late this year. Your horse recovered and you finished plowing before the rain started.

field.name: FDBK19
field.text: You were lucky this time. The horses recovered and you finished plowing before the snow started.

field.name: NoBuild
field.text: You need more money to do this.

field.name: NoSell
field.text: You have nothing to sell.

field.name: GoBank
field.text: Go to the bank to collect your money.

field.name: Hints
field.text:
2,10,11,16,18,22
Click on the squares you want to plow. Each square
represents 20 acres. Decide how many workers to hire
by clicking on the arrows in the Workers box. To start 
plowing, click on OK. To leave the fields without plowing,
click on Cancel. Tip: In the spring try to finish plowing
your fields by the end of May, before the heavy summer
rains start and the ground becomes too muddy for plowing.
In the fall, try to finish plowing before the first frost,
which comes in early October.
Once you have finished plowing your field, decide which 
seeds to plant. Make sure that you have bought enough 
seeds before you start planting. To plant, drag the seeds
 from the Seeds in Storage to the square you want to plant.
To start planting, click on OK. 
To leave the field without planting, click on Cancel.

Decide how many workers to hire by clicking on the arrows
 in the Workers box. Tip: Try to finish harvesting winter wheat 
in time to prepare your fields for planting summer crops. 
Try to finish harvesting summer crops in time to prepare
 your fields for planting winter wheat.

calendarExtra.text:
Now you are a homestead farmer who is successful
in business. What do you want to do next?
    
       I want to

       keep farming my homestead and remain 
       successful in business.

       keep farming my homestead and become mayor.

       let my son take over the homestead so I can 
       retire in town.

goalLists.name: ListM8
goalLists.text:
TOWN OF LONGVIEW
                                             BUFFALO COUNTY, KANSAS

 The people of Longview want to know where you stand.
 Click on the issues you support :

        America should get involved in the war in Europe.
       
        All women in America should be allowed to vote.
     
        Kansas should remain a "dry" state.    
         
        The federal government should own and operate the railroads.
       
        Ranchers should be put in jail for grazing their cattle on farmland. 
       
        Citizens under 18 years of age should be allowed to carry pistols in town.

Hi there, neighbor. I have bad news for you.
My grain elevator is full, so I can't buy your grain. Because of the railroad strike, I can't ship the grain
back east. Come back when the strike is finished.

bank.name: Telegram
bank.text:
TELEGRAM 
FROM: O'Grady Town
TO: dfgg

I have some bad news for you. On my way to O'Grady, 
I was caught in a sudden rainstorm. Part of your crop was ruined. I could only sell some of it. You can get your money from the cashier at the bank. I hope next time we'll have better luck.

claimForm.text: STATE OF KANSAS / This Certifies that [First Name] [Last Name] has paid ten dollars and filed a claim for 160 acres in Buffalo County, registered as LOT NUMBER 9474. According to the Homestead Act of 1862, whoever files a claim on public land to establish a homestead must be: • an American citizen or planning to become one • the head of a household • at least 21 years old. A claim filer who lives on and works this land for at least 5 years will become its owner. The claim filer must build a place to live and find a source of water. If the claim filer does not meet these conditions, the government may take away the land. [signature] Signature of Land Officer — APRIL 1, 1880 Date — Signature of Claim Filer
